Hexagonal cystine crystals support cystinuria, which increases cystine and dibasic amino-acid excretion. The pictured crystals must be verified before applying that explanation to the exception choice.

Preformed antibodies against graft antigens trigger complement-mediated vascular damage in hyperacute rejection. This antibody-mediated cytotoxic process is conventionally classified as type II hypersensitivity.
Serotonin metabolism produces 5-HIAA, measured in urine for selected serotonin-secreting neuroendocrine tumours. Diet, medicines and tumour characteristics affect interpretation.
H. pylori urease generates ammonia from urea, helping buffer its local gastric environment. This enzyme also underlies urea-based diagnostic tests.

Intestinal metabolism of choline can generate trimethylamine, which accumulates when FMO3 activity is inadequate. Dietary management needs supervision because choline is essential and excessive restriction can be harmful.
Mycoplasma lacks peptidoglycan and is intrinsically resistant to beta-lactam antibiotics. A drug targeting cell-wall synthesis has no corresponding structural target.
Chaperones assist protein folding and prevent inappropriate aggregation without determining the protein's amino-acid sequence. They can help refold stress-damaged proteins.
Holder or low-temperature long-time pasteurisation uses approximately sixty-three degrees Celsius for thirty minutes. It reduces pathogens without constituting sterilisation.
Fumarylacetoacetate hydrolase deficiency blocks the final step of tyrosine degradation. Toxic metabolites can damage liver and kidneys and increase hepatocellular-carcinoma risk.
GALT deficiency prevents normal galactose-1-phosphate processing. Milk feeding can precipitate hepatic illness, cataracts and susceptibility to serious infection.
A minus cylinder with a plano spherical component can correct simple myopic astigmatism. One principal meridian remains emmetropic while the other requires negative power.
Pharmacological niacin can worsen glycaemic control, which matters in diabetes. The effect requires monitoring rather than treating every diabetic patient as having an absolute contraindication.
Moraxella lacunata is the classic cause of angular blepharoconjunctivitis, affecting the lid angles. Clinical presentation and microbiology help distinguish other chronic conjunctival infections.
DNA methylation and histone modifications can change gene expression without altering the underlying nucleotide sequence. These regulatory changes are described as epigenetic.
Chlamydia trachomatis is a common infectious cause of neonatal conjunctivitis in many settings. Local screening and prevention alter frequency, so a universal developed-country ranking is imprecise.
Normally LDH2 exceeds LDH1 in serum. An LDH1-dominant flipped pattern was historically used in myocardial-infarction assessment, but is neither specific nor preferred over troponin.
Enterovirus 70 can cause outbreaks of acute haemorrhagic conjunctivitis. Coxsackievirus A24 variant is another recognised cause, so the association is not exclusive.
Ischaemic CRVO can drive VEGF-mediated iris and angle neovascularisation, causing neovascular glaucoma. The traditional hundred-day label describes a recognised risk period, not an exact deadline.
Right lateral rectus and left medial rectus act together during rightward conjugate gaze. Yoke muscles receive coordinated innervation to move both eyes in the same direction.

Pain and reduced vision soon after cataract surgery can indicate endophthalmitis requiring urgent ophthalmic assessment. The image, visual acuity and examination determine intravitreal treatment and whether vitrectomy is needed.

Diabetic microvascular third-nerve palsy can cause ptosis and extraocular weakness, often sparing the pupil. Most common feature is an imprecise ranking, and pupil sparing does not alone exclude compression.
The thin orbital floor commonly fractures after blunt trauma, allowing tissue herniation into the maxillary sinus. The medial wall can also be involved.

Small irregular pupils that accommodate but respond poorly to light describe light-near dissociation associated with neurosyphilis. Other causes exist, so examination and appropriate testing are necessary.
White-centred retinal haemorrhages can occur with leukaemia and several systemic illnesses, including endocarditis. They are not specific for a single diagnosis.

Presbyopia reflects declining accommodative reserve and is treated with an appropriate near addition. Age alone does not establish a universal plus-three-dioptre prescription; working distance and refraction matter.
De Quervain tenosynovitis affects abductor pollicis longus and extensor pollicis brevis in the first dorsal compartment at the radial wrist.

A darkening finger after injury can indicate compromised circulation and demands urgent assessment. Neurovascular compromise takes priority over uncomplicated abrasions or stable fracture classification.
Haematogenous dissemination of tuberculosis can produce numerous small millet-like lesions. Imaging and microbiological assessment are needed before confirming the pictured diagnosis.

The Chadha committee addressed integration of malaria surveillance with basic health services and multipurpose staffing. Population norms and committee recommendations should be checked against the historical report rather than current PHC standards.

Periventricular calcification, microcephaly and petechiae suggest congenital CMV. Urine or saliva nucleic-acid testing within the early neonatal diagnostic window can establish congenital infection; late positivity may not distinguish postnatal acquisition.

Sprengel deformity is congenital elevation of the scapula and may accompany cervical vertebral anomalies and other skeletal abnormalities. Dextrocardia is not a classic defining association in the usual teaching list.
Gastric adenocarcinoma is a malignant gland-forming epithelial tumour. Gastric neuroendocrine tumours arise from specialised epithelial neuroendocrine cells.
Distal forearm fractures are very common in children, often after falls onto an outstretched hand. Frequency depends on age and whether individual bones or anatomical regions are counted.
Facial angiofibromas are characteristic of tuberous sclerosis, whereas cafe-au-lait macules and neurofibromas suggest NF1. The pictured lesion must establish which syndrome the exception concerns.

Designated microscopy centres were peripheral diagnostic units in the older RNTCP structure. Contemporary NTEP diagnosis includes expanding molecular testing, so this organisational answer requires its historical context.

Classic 21-hydroxylase deficiency can virilise external genitalia in a 46,XX infant through excess adrenal androgens. The older option terminology should be explained using current DSD language rather than repeated uncritically.
Persistent bone infection can produce sequestrum, involucrum and chronic sinus formation after trauma. The radiograph is required to distinguish these changes from malignancy and other lesions.
TRALI is an acute transfusion-associated respiratory syndrome developing during or within six hours of transfusion. Assessment must distinguish it from circulatory overload and other lung injury.
The historical Factories Act prohibited employment of children below fourteen in factories. The age threshold belongs to that statutory framework.

Intra-articular disease often hurts during both active and passive movement. Periarticular lesions may predominantly hurt with specific active or resisted actions, although painless passive movement is not an absolute diagnostic rule.
A cortical fragment can fall into the fluid-filled cavity of a unicameral bone cyst after fracture. This supports a simple bone cyst in the appropriate imaging setting.
A midline lumbosacral hair tuft may mark occult spinal dysraphism. Imaging and neurological assessment are needed; the skin sign alone does not distinguish every underlying spinal anomaly.
Iodine requirements rise during lactation because iodine is secreted in breast milk to support infant thyroid-hormone production. Adequate maternal intake supports both maternal and infant needs.

references.title: WHO/UNICEF: iodine nutrition during pregnancy and lactation

records.explanation: Perilunate dislocation generally preserves radius-lunate alignment while displacing the capitate. A lunate displaced anteriorly from the radius instead describes lunate dislocation and is the intended incorrect statement.

Aqueductal obstruction can cause noncommunicating hydrocephalus with enlargement upstream. Congenital ventriculomegaly has several causes, and the most common depends on the population and associated malformations.

Neonatal epinephrine is considered when severe bradycardia persists despite effective ventilation and coordinated compressions under the resuscitation algorithm. Establishing adequate ventilation takes priority because most neonatal bradycardia is respiratory.
Nonparametric methods can be useful when distributional assumptions of a parametric method are unsuitable. They are not exclusively for skewed data, and each test still has assumptions.
Impaired platelet adhesion in von Willebrand disease can prolong bleeding time, an older test. Modern diagnosis instead uses appropriate VWF antigen, activity and related assays.
A fall on an outstretched hand can fracture the distal radius or scaphoid.

ATM-related ataxia-telangiectasia commonly includes progressive ataxia, telangiectasia, immunodeficiency, increased cancer risk and elevated AFP. It is usually autosomal recessive rather than dominant.

Article 21 of the Indian Constitution protects life and personal liberty. Its interpretation includes extensive judicial development; the provision should not be confused with Article 21A on education.
Hypertrophic nonunion usually retains biological healing activity but lacks adequate mechanical stability. Correcting stability is central, while infection and alignment also require assessment.
Measles can produce multinucleated Warthin-Finkeldey giant cells in lymphoid tissue. Their syncytial appearance reflects virus-associated cell fusion.

Measles elimination requires very high, sustained two-dose coverage, generally at least ninety-five percent in every area. A calculated threshold such as ninety-six percent depends on transmission assumptions and is not a universal WHO eradication figure.
Common red-green colour-vision deficiency is X-linked. The other listed classic conditions, cystic fibrosis, sickle-cell disease and common thalassaemias, are generally autosomal recessive.
Older childhood age, including age ten or above in common risk schemes, can predict higher-risk ALL. Genetics, initial white count and treatment response are also major prognostic determinants.
Growth hormone stimulates hepatic IGF-1 production, which mediates many systemic growth effects. Other tissues also produce IGF locally for paracrine actions.

Treatment comparisons require the observed effect size, its uncertainty and the study design. A p-value describes compatibility with a specified null hypothesis and does not independently give the magnitude or direction of benefit.
Cardiac allograft vasculopathy causes diffuse coronary vascular narrowing after transplantation and limits long-term graft survival. Immune and nonimmune factors both contribute.
Roseola is usually caused by human herpesvirus 6 or 7. Parvovirus B19 instead causes erythema infectiosum, fetal anaemia or hydrops and transient aplastic crises.

Prosopagnosia impairs recognition of familiar faces despite adequate basic vision. Dysfunction commonly involves occipitotemporal face-processing networks rather than general object identification alone.

Ovotesticular differences of sex development involve both ovarian and testicular tissue, often with a 46,XX karyotype. The historical terminology in the source should not replace current respectful terminology.
Myotonic dystrophy type 1 involves a CTG expansion in DMPK on chromosome 19. Type 2 involves a different repeat expansion on chromosome 3.
The thick ascending limb reabsorbs salt without accompanying water, contributing to the medullary concentration gradient. Thin ascending segments also permit passive salt transport.

references.title: Primary renal transport study: passive sodium transport in ascending thin limb

records.explanation: Bilateral vestibular schwannomas are characteristic of NF2-related schwannomatosis. NF1 instead features findings such as cafe-au-lait macules, neurofibromas and specific bone lesions; brain tumour alone is imprecise.

Some dehydration is commonly treated with weight-based ORS over four hours and reassessment. Age-based volume ranges are approximations; the child's weight, ability to drink and severity determine the actual plan.

references.title: WHO Pocket Book: diarrhoea treatment plan C

records.explanation: Pathogenic PTEN variants impair a tumour-suppressor pathway controlling cellular growth. Cowden syndrome forms part of PTEN hamartoma tumour syndrome.
SGLT1 couples luminal glucose entry to the sodium gradient, making uptake secondary active transport. GLUT2-mediated basolateral exit is facilitated diffusion and is a separate step.
Profound undernutrition is life-threatening, but no single BMI is universally lethal. Survival and treatment urgency depend on physiology, complications and the clinical course.

Medicines are important causes of acquired agranulocytosis, but infection, immune disease and marrow pathology also matter. A universal most-common ranking requires a defined population and diagnostic setting.
Breslow thickness measures melanoma invasion depth and informs prognosis. It is not a measurement of total body-fat percentage, unlike appropriate anthropometric or body-composition methods.
Relative risk compares the disease risk in an exposed group with risk in an unexposed group over a defined period. It differs from the odds ratio.
Pancreatic-head tumours commonly obstruct the distal bile duct and cause jaundice. Body or tail tumours often present later with pain or weight loss, so jaundice is less characteristic.

Net reproduction depends on fertility, mortality and population-specific patterns of contraceptive use. A fixed couple-protection percentage does not universally guarantee replacement-level reproduction.
Bartonella henselae infection can produce suppurative lymphadenitis with stellate granulomas. Exposure history and appropriate testing help distinguish other granulomatous infections.
Nikshay is India's digital tuberculosis notification and programme-management platform. The older RNTCP programme name has since changed to NTEP.

Cytotoxic wastes require authorised return or specialised treatment such as high-temperature incineration. Generic incineration without specified standards is incomplete, and ordinary disposal methods should not be substituted.
Chronic anthraquinone laxative exposure, such as senna, can cause pigment-laden macrophages in colonic mucosa. The pigmentation is lipofuscin-like rather than true melanin.

Sensitivity equals true positives divided by all people with disease. Ninety screen positives and one hundred gold-standard positives imply ninety percent only if all ninety screen positives are true positives.
Nitrates increase nitric-oxide signalling and PDE5 inhibitors reduce cGMP breakdown. Combining them can produce profound hypotension and is contraindicated within the relevant exposure interval.
Under steady-state assumptions for an uncommon disease, prevalence approximates incidence multiplied by average duration. Four per thousand per year times two years gives eight per thousand.
Linezolid inhibits bacterial protein synthesis by preventing initiation-complex formation. It is generally bacteriostatic against staphylococci and enterococci, although activity varies by organism.
Emtricitabine inhibits HIV reverse transcription and also has anti-HBV activity. The separately listed enfuvirtide, abacavir and ritonavir do not provide equivalent HBV treatment activity.

Secondary attack rate measures new cases among susceptible contacts after exposure to a primary case, within the relevant follow-up interval. The denominator excludes those already immune or primary cases.

A body-surface-area-based hydrocortisone replacement figure is fundamentally different from milligrams per kilogram. Appropriate replacement depends on age, diagnosis and guideline; stress dosing is a separate regimen.

references.title: Endocrine Society: primary adrenal insufficiency guideline

records.explanation: Dissolved calcium and magnesium salts cause hardness. Calcium carbonate's poor solubility distinguishes it from soluble bicarbonates, but hardness is itself often expressed as calcium-carbonate equivalents.
Doxycycline is a standard treatment option for scrub typhus. Age, pregnancy, severity and local guidance can affect drug selection, including use of azithromycin in appropriate situations.
Quinidine blocks cardiac repolarising potassium currents and can prolong QT, increasing torsades risk. Electrolytes, interactions and other QT-prolonging medicines influence the risk.

Droplet nuclei can remain suspended and produce airborne transmission, conventionally classified as indirect. This differs from short-range direct droplet spread despite both originating in respiratory secretions.
Sacubitril is converted to a neprilysin inhibitor that reduces breakdown of natriuretic peptides. It is used with valsartan, not as an ACE inhibitor.

Different live injectable or intranasal vaccines are generally given together or at least twenty-eight days apart. Oral live vaccines have exceptions; four weeks is not a universal rule for all vaccines.

references.title: CDC: timing and spacing of immunobiologics

records.explanation: Lepirudin is a direct thrombin inhibitor whose anticoagulant effect was monitored using coagulation assays such as aPTT. It is a historical drug example rather than a current universal prescribing recommendation.
Lymphocyte-predominant cells have folded popcorn-like nuclei and a B-cell phenotype. They support nodular lymphocyte-predominant disease rather than classical Hodgkin lymphoma.

The traditional Indian endemic focus included Bihar and parts of neighbouring eastern states. Disease distribution and elimination status change, so this historical geography exception is not a timeless surveillance claim.
Propranolol is not a usual first-line agent for pregnancy hypertension, but it may be used for other maternal indications.
Risperidone blocks dopamine D2 receptors in the tuberoinfundibular pathway, removing dopamine's inhibition of prolactin release. The effect varies with dose and individual susceptibility.
Ecological studies analyse groups or populations rather than individual-level exposure-outcome pairs. Associations at group level need not hold for individuals, creating ecological-fallacy risk.
When pH equals pKa, the relevant protonated and unprotonated forms occur in equal concentrations. For a simple monoprotic drug this means equal ionised and unionised fractions.
Betamethasone is an antenatal corticosteroid used to improve outcomes when preterm birth is likely within recommended circumstances. Gestational age, infection and timing determine suitability.
Amphotericin B binds fungal membrane ergosterol and disrupts membrane integrity. Its target is the cell membrane rather than the fungal cell wall.

Strontium ranelate was described as affecting both formation and resorption. Cardiovascular and other safety concerns restrict its clinical role, so the pharmacology answer is not a treatment recommendation.
Valproate can reduce choreiform movements in Sydenham chorea. Treatment selection also considers adverse effects, pregnancy potential, severity and management of rheumatic disease.
Transient fine transverse folds producing a feline oesophagus can associate with reflux.
Basiliximab binds CD25, the IL-2 receptor alpha chain on activated T cells, inhibiting IL-2-driven proliferation during transplant immunosuppression.
The superior vena cava drains upper-body systemic venous blood into the right atrium. Its CT position and enhancement distinguish it from adjacent arteries; the marked image must be reviewed.

Pirenzepine preferentially blocks muscarinic M1 receptors and historically reduced gastric acid secretion. Contemporary peptic-ulcer treatment generally uses other acid suppression and cause-directed therapy.

Piperacillin-tazobactam may show laboratory activity against some ESBL producers, but is not universally appropriate. Invasive infection and resistance mechanisms often favour other agents under current guidance.
Metyrapone inhibits adrenal 11-beta-hydroxylase, reducing cortisol synthesis. Mifepristone instead antagonises glucocorticoid receptors rather than directly blocking hormone synthesis.
Hyperparathyroid bone resorption can produce granular skull demineralisation described as salt-and-pepper change. Biochemistry and the complete imaging pattern are needed for diagnosis.
Hydralazine reduces arterial afterload while isosorbide dinitrate reduces venous preload through nitric-oxide signalling. The combination has defined roles in selected heart-failure patients.
Colchicine binds tubulin and disrupts microtubule-dependent neutrophil functions, reducing inflammation. It does not lower urate by inhibiting its synthesis.
Water-soluble iodinated contrast can demonstrate an oesophageal leak while limiting complications from extraluminal barium. Contrast selection also accounts for aspiration risk and test sensitivity.
Prasugrel is metabolically converted to an active inhibitor of platelet P2Y12 receptors. This antiplatelet effect must be considered with bleeding risk and its contraindications.
Dissection creates a false lumen within the aortic wall. Imaging must define whether the ascending aorta is involved because classification and urgent management depend on that distinction.
Apixaban directly inhibits activated factor X, reducing thrombin generation and clot formation. It does not require antithrombin to exert this effect.

Oestrogen exposure is associated with hepatocellular adenoma, but liver imaging must distinguish it from focal nodular hyperplasia and other masses. Risk assessment also depends on lesion subtype and size.
Vertebral or PICA territory infarction can damage the lateral medulla, producing crossed sensory findings, vestibular symptoms, dysphagia and ipsilateral Horner syndrome.

Large volumes of dilute urine with inadequate vasopressin signalling can reflect central diabetes insipidus. Osmolality testing and the actual MRI findings are needed; a hormone concentration alone is difficult to interpret.
A vein-of-Galen-region arteriovenous malformation involves abnormal high-flow embryonic venous connections. The MRI or angiographic pattern is essential to verify this diagnosis.
Visible painless haematuria is a common presenting symptom of bladder cancer. It also has benign causes, so appropriate urinary-tract evaluation is required rather than assuming the diagnosis.
A single developed Mullerian duct can produce a unicornuate uterine cavity. Imaging must evaluate the external contour and any rudimentary horn before classifying the anomaly.
Protons deposit much of their energy near the end of their range, creating a Bragg peak. Planning can use this property to reduce dose beyond the target.
Hysterosalpingography outlines the uterine cavity and fallopian tubes with contrast and can assess tubal spill. The image and contrast distribution are needed to confirm the study.

Pyrogenic cytokines induce hypothalamic prostaglandin signalling to raise the temperature set point. Histamine primarily contributes vascular permeability and immediate inflammatory responses rather than being a principal endogenous pyrogen.
A prolactin level above two hundred micrograms per litre raises suspicion of prolactinoma but is not invariably diagnostic. Drugs, assays, other causes and imaging still require assessment.
Anaplasia means loss of differentiation, often with pleomorphism and abnormal nuclear features. It differs from metaplasia, which substitutes one mature cell type for another.
The superior mesenteric artery arises anteriorly from the abdominal aorta below the coeliac origin and supplies midgut structures. Its labelled angiographic course must be checked.
C3b coats microbial surfaces and promotes recognition by complement receptors on phagocytes. C3a and C5a instead have prominent inflammatory signalling roles.

Late prosthetic-valve endocarditis can involve streptococci, staphylococci and enterococci, resembling native-valve microbiology more than early postoperative infection. Timing alone cannot reliably identify the organism.
PNH cells lack GPI-anchored complement regulators, including CD55 and CD59. Flow cytometry demonstrates deficient expression; CD59 positivity itself is not the defining abnormality.
Subcutaneous rheumatoid nodules are a classic extra-articular feature, particularly in seropositive disease. Their frequency depends on disease severity, treatment and the population studied.

Whipple disease can produce PAS-positive macrophages in small-intestinal lamina propria containing bacterial material. Confirmation uses the broader histological and microbiological context, since PAS positivity is not exclusive.
Factor V Leiden produces resistance to activated protein C, reducing normal anticoagulant inactivation of factor V and increasing venous-thrombosis susceptibility.
Craniopharyngioma often occupies the sellar-suprasellar region and may contain cystic and calcified components. The scan is needed to distinguish other pituitary-region lesions.
In the Berlin framework, moderate ARDS has a PaO2/FiO2 ratio above one hundred and at most two hundred with required positive pressure. Two hundred to three hundred denotes mild disease.
ATP7A dysfunction impairs copper transport in Menkes disease, producing deficient copper delivery to tissues. Neurological deterioration and abnormal hair are characteristic clues.

Tumour size historically helped distinguish small papillary renal adenomas from carcinomas. Malignant behaviour is assessed using the complete pathological classification, grade and stage rather than size alone.
Small-vessel vasculitis can affect skin, kidneys and peripheral nerves. ANCA testing supports selected diagnoses but requires clinical correlation and sometimes tissue biopsy.
Increased epithelial sodium-channel activity causes sodium retention, hypertension and potassium-hydrogen loss. Renin and aldosterone are typically suppressed, unlike primary aldosteronism.
Untreated HIV often progresses over years, with a historically quoted median near a decade. Modern ART greatly changes this course, and individual progression varies substantially.

Maternal antibodies can persist in infants, so virological nucleic-acid testing is used for early diagnosis. Sampling timing, repeat confirmation and breastfeeding exposure follow the national infant-testing algorithm.
Antibodies commonly target postsynaptic nicotinic acetylcholine receptors, reducing effective neuromuscular transmission. Other patients have antibodies to proteins such as MuSK instead.

Weber syndrome combines ipsilateral third-nerve palsy with contralateral corticospinal or corticobulbar weakness. Ipsilateral lower-facial paralysis is therefore inconsistent with the classic crossed motor pattern.

Allergic bronchopulmonary aspergillosis involves Aspergillus hypersensitivity and commonly elevated total IgE. Diagnosis combines sensitisation testing, immunological findings and compatible clinical or imaging features.
Vaso-occlusion in the small bones of hands and feet can cause painful swelling in young children with sickle-cell disease, termed dactylitis.

A pressure of at least one hundred sixty over one hundred generally warrants prompt treatment, but lower confirmed pressures can also warrant medication. The threshold depends on the named guideline, risk and follow-up assessment.
Hepatitis C is strongly associated with mixed cryoglobulinaemia, which can cause purpura, neuropathy and glomerular disease. Other infections, autoimmune disorders and malignancies are alternatives.

Central respiratory depression requires restoration of ventilation and treatment of the cause. Oxygen can correct hypoxaemia but does not by itself remove carbon dioxide or resolve airway obstruction.
Cord hemisection causes ipsilateral motor and dorsal-column deficits below the lesion, with contralateral pain-temperature loss beginning somewhat below the injured segment.
Graves hyperthyroidism usually suppresses TSH through negative feedback while raising free thyroid hormones. Exceptions and assay interference require clinical and biochemical correlation.

Takotsubo syndrome produces transient ventricular dysfunction often extending beyond one coronary distribution. Coronary disease and other causes must still be evaluated; ECG alone does not establish it.
A Kayser-Fleischer ring would support investigation for Wilson disease, including ceruloplasmin and copper studies.
Abacavir lacks clinically useful anti-HBV activity. It can still be part of an appropriate HIV regimen in selected coinfected patients if adequate separate HBV-active treatment is included.
Early ventricular contraction bulges the closed tricuspid valve toward the right atrium, contributing to the jugular c wave during isovolumetric contraction.

ICDs prevent sudden arrhythmic death in selected survivors of ventricular arrhythmia and high-risk cardiac disease. Acute coronary syndrome with low ejection fraction alone does not imply immediate implantation.

Endothelin-1 generally promotes vasoconstriction and can contribute bronchoconstriction and proliferative effects. Bronchodilation is not its characteristic direct action, although endothelial responses can vary by receptor context.
Hypokalaemia can alter atrial and ventricular repolarisation and has been associated with prominent P waves. ECG interpretation must also consider true right-atrial abnormality and other causes.
Raised extracellular potassium directly stimulates adrenal zona-glomerulosa aldosterone secretion. Angiotensin II is another major regulator, while ACTH has a smaller acute influence.
Nitric oxide activates soluble guanylate cyclase in smooth muscle, increasing cGMP. Downstream signalling lowers contractile activity and promotes vasodilatation.

Very severe airflow obstruction corresponds to FEV1 below thirty percent predicted after confirming persistent obstruction. Spirometric grade must be separated from current symptom-exacerbation treatment grouping.

Maastricht category III denotes controlled donation after circulatory death following planned withdrawal of life-sustaining treatment and subsequent circulatory arrest. It differs from uncontrolled failed-resuscitation categories.

Hypothyroidism can cause bradycardia and occasionally clinically important atrioventricular block. Other cardiac, drug and electrolyte causes must be considered rather than attributing a block to thyroid disease alone.
Ciprofloxacin can be used for eligible close contacts when local resistance patterns permit. Broad mass prophylaxis is not routine, and resistance may require a different recommended agent.
Chordoma arises from notochordal remnants, typically along the axial skeleton. This developmental origin helps explain its predilection for sacral and clival regions.
Torus tubarius is the mucosal elevation produced by auditory-tube cartilage near its pharyngeal opening on the lateral nasopharyngeal wall. It is not itself a separate tonsil.
Vocal nodules classically develop near the junction of the anterior one-third and posterior two-thirds of the vocal fold. Repeated phonotrauma contributes to their formation.
Ventilation without perfusion produces an infinite ventilation-perfusion ratio and alveolar dead space. Without blood flow, that unit contributes no blood-gas exchange.
DMT1 transports ferrous iron across the apical enterocyte membrane. Ferroportin exports iron basolaterally into the circulation after intracellular processing.
Importins recognise nuclear-localisation signals and participate in transport through nuclear pores. Ran GTPase supplies directionality through its compartment-specific nucleotide state.

The early ebb phase is characterised by depressed perfusion and metabolic activity; the later flow phase is hypermetabolic and catabolic. Inflammatory activation overlaps phases, so rigid timing claims are simplified.

Sympathetic activation during shock can increase renal arteriolar resistance and reduce renal perfusion. The fragment increasing afferent arteriole should mean increased resistance, not increased vessel diameter.
Many oculocutaneous albinism forms are autosomal recessive, whereas ocular albinism can be X-linked. The subtype matters before assigning inheritance universally.
Rotation around the dens at the atlanto-axial complex permits much of the head's side-to-side turning movement.
OTC deficiency impairs ureagenesis, increasing ammonia and glutamine formation. Other urea-cycle defects also elevate glutamine; distinguishing them requires additional biochemical findings.
The circumflex usually branches from the left main coronary artery. Coronary dominance describes posterior descending supply and does not ordinarily change this parent vessel.
Methionine supplies methyl groups through S-adenosylmethionine for PNMT-mediated conversion of noradrenaline to adrenaline.
Failure of physiologically herniated midgut to return normally leaves bowel within a membrane-covered umbilical defect, producing an omphalocele.
Projection fibres connect cerebral cortex with lower neural structures. The marked tract must be inspected before distinguishing projection from association or commissural fibres.
The modern hepatocystic triangle is bounded by the cystic duct, common hepatic duct and inferior liver surface. The gallbladder itself is not a standard boundary; historical definitions differ.
The umbilical region is conventionally associated with T10. The marked skin region is required to confirm that this landmark is what the question depicts.
Extensor carpi radialis muscles extend and radially deviate the wrist. Their marked anatomical course must be seen to distinguish them from adjacent extensors.
The median nerve supplies several forearm flexors and thenar muscles, with recognised exceptions. The labelled structure is essential to verify its actual innervation.
The radial nerve supplies dorsal radial hand sensation, classically including the first dorsal web space. The arrow's exact location determines whether this applies.
Cantlie's plane runs approximately from the gallbladder fossa to the inferior vena cava and separates functional right and left hepatic territories.
Epidermis derives from ectoderm, whereas most dermis derives from mesoderm, with neural-crest contributions in craniofacial regions. General ectodermal origin for dermis is therefore incorrect.
External-oblique aponeurosis contributes several inguinal structures. Linea semilunaris marks the rectus sheath's lateral boundary and is not simply an external-oblique derivative alone.
Prostatic median-lobe enlargement can elevate bladder-neck mucosa and form the uvula vesicae. The relationship helps explain bladder-outlet obstruction.
Common fibular nerve injury can weaken dorsiflexion and produce foot drop. L5 radiculopathy and other lesions can also do so; the full neurological pattern localises the injury.
De Quervain disease involves abductor pollicis longus and extensor pollicis brevis in the first dorsal wrist compartment.
The fornix is a major hippocampal output pathway connecting with diencephalic structures. The labelled image must establish that tract rather than adjacent commissures.
Levator veli palatini is supplied through the pharyngeal plexus and is not a first-arch muscle. Tensor veli palatini belongs to the first-arch group.
Nondepolarising blockers competitively inhibit postsynaptic nicotinic acetylcholine receptors, reducing neuromuscular transmission without themselves ensuring anaesthesia.
Etomidate tends to preserve haemodynamic stability better than several induction agents. It is not devoid of cardiovascular effects and can suppress adrenal steroid synthesis.
Desflurane's pungency and airway irritation make it unsuitable for routine inhalational induction, particularly in children. Sevoflurane is less irritating.
Ketamine formulations generally cause less injection discomfort than agents such as propofol or etomidate. Saying injection is never painful would overstate the comparison.
Bispectral index processes EEG information to help assess hypnotic drug effect. It supplements clinical monitoring and does not directly measure analgesia or guarantee absence of awareness.
A pulse oximeter estimates peripheral arterial oxygen saturation from pulsatile light absorption. The pictured device must be confirmed, and saturation does not directly measure ventilation.
Acute fatty liver of pregnancy usually occurs in the third trimester or around delivery and can rapidly cause metabolic and hepatic failure.
Oestrogen increases vaginal epithelial glycogen, supporting lactobacillary metabolism and an acidic environment. Pregnancy also increases vascularity and physiological discharge.
A fasting plasma glucose at or above 126 mg/dL meets a standard diabetes threshold, usually requiring confirmation unless unequivocal. A fetal malformation alone does not establish maternal diabetes.
Endometrial glands and stroma within myometrium can cause diffuse uterine enlargement, pain and myometrial cysts, supporting adenomyosis.
Diaphragmatic elevation during pregnancy reduces expiratory reserve and residual volumes, lowering functional residual capacity despite increased ventilation.
Cardiac disease is not automatically a contraindication to labour induction. Timing and method require lesion-specific maternal assessment and multidisciplinary planning.
Placental relationship to the internal cervical os determines the diagnosis. Historical grade III terminology requires the actual diagram and differs from current ultrasound-based descriptions.
A soft flow-related systolic ejection murmur can be physiological in pregnancy. A pansystolic murmur warrants assessment for valvular or structural disease.
Fibroid torsion and red degeneration can both cause acute pain. Pedunculation, examination and imaging are needed; normal white count alone does not reliably distinguish them.
Dicloxacillin can treat susceptible bacterial mastitis, but many inflammatory cases initially need supportive management. Abscess, severity and local resistance change treatment.
Fetal urine becomes a major amniotic-fluid contributor during the second half of pregnancy. Fetal swallowing and intramembranous pathways also regulate volume.
Lower AMH suggests a smaller recruitable follicle pool. A threshold near one depends on units, assay and clinical purpose and does not alone establish infertility.

Carboprost may be repeated to a protocol-defined maximum cumulative dose in postpartum haemorrhage. Route, contraindications and prior doses must be confirmed; the number is not a single injection dose.

A partial hydatidiform mole is an abnormal gestation with malignant potential, but is not automatically gestational trophoblastic neoplasia. Persistent disease is established through clinical and hCG criteria.
Maternal hyperglycaemia can produce fetal hyperinsulinaemia and excess growth, but appearance alone is insufficient to diagnose maternal diabetes. The image and pregnancy data are needed.
After ovulation, corpus-luteal progesterone converts proliferative endometrium into a secretory lining suitable for implantation.
Oestrogen-containing combined contraception can increase venous thrombosis risk. Active or high-risk thromboembolic disease commonly precludes use, according to the applicable eligibility criteria.
Partial moles are usually diandric triploid conceptions, often 69,XXY. Not every partial mole has the identical sex-chromosome complement.
Vaginal hysterectomy with appropriate support repair is an option for advanced prolapse. Symptoms, uterine preservation preferences, fitness and alternative repairs determine the best treatment.
Emergency contraception uses a single 30-mg ulipristal dose under its approved regimen. This differs from dosing historically studied for other indications.
Nuchal translucency is assessed in a defined first-trimester crown-rump-length window, usually around eleven to thirteen weeks plus six days. Dating and technique matter.

Magnesium sulphate prevents or treats eclamptic seizures and provides fetal neuroprotection in selected imminent preterm births. Antenatal corticosteroids, rather than magnesium, principally promote lung maturation.
A well-flexed vertex presents the suboccipitobregmatic diameter. Deflexion presents larger diameters that can impede descent.
Low-dose aspirin plus heparin is commonly used for qualifying obstetric antiphospholipid syndrome. Diagnostic criteria and prior thrombosis determine the exact regimen and monitoring.

Persistent postpartum pelvic infection may require broad antimicrobial treatment and consideration of anticoagulation when septic thrombophlebitis is diagnosed. Diagnosis and treatment duration need specialist assessment.
Local vaginal oestrogen can improve symptomatic atrophic vulvovaginal changes when appropriate. Alternative causes of itching and patient-specific contraindications require assessment first.
Pruritic eczema with an atopic family history supports atopic dermatitis. The distribution and photographed morphology are needed to confirm the diagnosis.
Certain substituted phenols, including para-tertiary-butylphenol, can damage melanocytes and cause contact leukoderma. Exposure history distinguishes it from other depigmenting disorders.
Infections can trigger inflammatory eruptions by activating immune responses. The association depends on the organism, timing and the particular skin disorder.
Trichomonas can produce frothy discharge and punctate cervical or vaginal erythema. A nitroimidazole such as metronidazole treats infection, with partner management and appropriate testing.
Herpes zoster can involve mucosa supplied by an affected sensory distribution.
Candida can cause inflamed moist skin folds with peripheral satellite lesions. The photograph and examination help distinguish irritant intertrigo and dermatophyte infection.
Nail-matrix abnormalities in psoriasis commonly produce pitting. Other disorders can pit nails too, so the associated pictured condition must be confirmed.
Velvety thickened hyperpigmented skin in flexures can indicate acanthosis nigricans. Causes include insulin resistance and less commonly paraneoplastic disease, depending on presentation.
Peroxisomal dysfunction impairs very-long-chain-fatty-acid breakdown, causing accumulation. Long-chain alone is less precise than very-long-chain and should not blur the metabolic distinction.
Ammonia detoxification draws alpha-ketoglutarate toward glutamate and glutamine formation, potentially reducing available TCA-cycle intermediates and cerebral energy metabolism.
Achondroplasia typically results from an activating FGFR3 variant with autosomal-dominant inheritance. Many cases arise through a new variant rather than an affected parent.
Lysyl oxidase requires copper for collagen and elastin cross-linking. Copper transport defects in Menkes disease impair this and other copper-dependent functions.
Arginine supplies urea-cycle nitrogen, nitric-oxide synthesis and a guanidino group for creatine synthesis. Creatinine then forms from creatine-related compounds.
Human mitochondrial DNA is generally inherited maternally. Heteroplasmy and tissue-specific energy requirements influence expression of mitochondrial genetic disease.
Lipoprotein lipase normally hydrolyses triglycerides in chylomicrons and VLDL. Deficiency markedly impairs postprandial chylomicron clearance and can cause severe hypertriglyceridaemia.
Wilson disease can cause proximal renal tubular dysfunction, including aminoaciduria. Renal manifestations are considered alongside hepatic, neurological and copper-metabolism findings.
Fatty-acid synthesis uses NADPH as reducing power during chain elongation. NADH instead principally carries electrons for energy generation through oxidative pathways.

Traditional tuberculous otitis descriptions include relatively painless persistent discharge, multiple perforations and disproportionate hearing loss. Pain can still occur with complications, so absence is not absolute.
Keratin accumulation in the ear canal can cause severe pain, conductive loss and canal widening.
Frontal-bone osteomyelitis with an overlying subperiosteal abscess produces Pott puffy tumour. Intracranial spread is a serious associated risk.
Papillomatosis can produce exophytic laryngeal lesions and voice or airway symptoms, commonly associated with HPV 6 or 11. The laryngoscopic image requires confirmation.
Inspiratory stridor generally points toward an extrathoracic airway obstruction, including supraglottic disease.
Buffered charcoal yeast extract supports Legionella growth by supplying needed nutrients, including cysteine and iron. Routine media may not recover it reliably.
Fever, jaundice and conjunctival suffusion suggest leptospirosis. Microscopic agglutination is a reference serological method, with timing and paired samples influencing interpretation.
Trichuris eggs are barrel-shaped with polar plugs. Heavy infection can cause colitis, tenesmus and rectal prolapse, particularly in children.
Parvovirus B19 suppresses erythroid precursors and can cause severe fetal anaemia and nonimmune hydrops, mimicking consequences of immune haemolytic disease.
Eczema, recurrent respiratory infection and relatively noninflamed staphylococcal abscesses suggest a hyper-IgE disorder. Genetic subtype and immune assessment are needed for confirmation.
Herpes-family infections can produce Cowdry type A intranuclear inclusions with characteristic nuclear changes. The finding is not exclusive to HSV without other diagnostic evidence.
The named manoeuvre must be identified from its actual positioning and purpose.
A plano sphere with a negative cylinder corrects simple myopic astigmatism, where only one principal meridian requires myopic correction.
Fasanella-Servat-type posterior procedures can correct selected mild ptosis with suitable muscle function. Horner syndrome also requires cause evaluation; this is not a universal first step.
Rod-cone degeneration typically reduces electroretinographic responses in retinitis pigmentosa. A normal ERG is therefore inconsistent with established widespread retinal dysfunction.
Fatigable levator weakness causes ptosis in myasthenia gravis, often worsening with sustained activity. Diplopia can accompany it through extraocular-muscle involvement.
Orbital-floor or medial-wall fracture can entrap tissue and restrict eye movements after trauma. CT is needed to verify the fracture and assess entrapment.
Pterygium is fibrovascular conjunctival growth extending onto the cornea, often associated with ultraviolet exposure. The image distinguishes it from pinguecula and other surface lesions.
Hypermetropia can drive excessive accommodation and associated convergence, producing accommodative esotropia. High myopia is not the classic refractive association.
Vincristine, etoposide and carboplatin form a recognised systemic retinoblastoma regimen. Contemporary treatment varies by stage, eye involvement and specialist local or intra-arterial options.
An Ex-PRESS device creates an aqueous drainage pathway in selected glaucoma surgery. The procedure image and glaucoma subtype are needed to judge whether the named implant and treatment fit.
A Maddox rod converts a point light into a line and helps assess ocular misalignment. The instrument photograph must be checked before confirming its identity.
Cover-uncover testing detects a manifest deviation by observing fixation shifts. Alternating cover testing dissociates fusion to assess total deviation; the actual sequence distinguishes them.
Postpubertal macro-orchidism is a recognised fragile-X feature. Micro-orchidism is therefore the intended exception rather than a characteristic sign.
Prostate cancer commonly produces osteoblastic skeletal metastases. Imaging appearances can be mixed, and other malignancies may also produce sclerotic lesions.
Iron overload can cause hepatic enlargement and increased skin pigmentation. Histological iron staining and systemic iron studies are needed to verify the pictured diagnosis.
HSV oesophagitis classically produces small well-defined punched-out ulcers. Endoscopic biopsy and appropriate testing distinguish it from CMV and other ulcerative disease.
Alpha-1-antitrypsin inhibits neutrophil elastase. Deficiency permits excessive alveolar connective-tissue injury and predisposes to emphysema, especially with smoking.
Barrett oesophagus increases risk of oesophageal adenocarcinoma rather than primarily squamous-cell carcinoma. Surveillance depends on dysplasia and the relevant guideline.
An extra chromosome 21 increases APP gene dosage and contributes to earlier Alzheimer neuropathology in Down syndrome. Clinical dementia risk rises with age.
A qualifying Coxiella burnetii blood culture or high phase-I antibody titre can fulfil a major microbiological endocarditis criterion. Apply the exact current criteria and diagnostic context.
Inflammasome-associated caspase-1 cleaves pro-IL-1 beta into its mature inflammatory form. This should be distinguished from IL-1 alpha biology.
Entamoeba histolytica invades colonic mucosa and spreads laterally within submucosa, creating characteristic flask-shaped ulcers.
IL-1 promotes fever partly through prostaglandin signalling at the hypothalamus. Fever reflects an elevated set point rather than uncontrolled heat accumulation alone.
BCL2 inhibits mitochondrial apoptotic pathways, helping cells survive. Other BCL2-family members can instead promote apoptosis.
Immune-mediated injury to medium arteries in polyarteritis nodosa can produce eosinophilic fibrinoid material within damaged vessel walls.
APOE epsilon4 increases Alzheimer-disease susceptibility but is neither necessary nor sufficient for diagnosis. Risk differs by genotype and ancestry.
Prolonged heavy alcohol exposure can damage myocardium and cause ventricular dilatation with impaired systolic function. Other cardiomyopathy causes still require assessment.
Follicular lymphoma commonly has an IGH-BCL2 rearrangement that increases anti-apoptotic BCL2 expression, permitting abnormal germinal-centre B-cell survival.
Langerhans-cell lesions can produce lytic bone abnormalities. The radiograph and tissue findings are needed; normal routine blood or urine tests do not confirm the diagnosis.
Repeated inflammation and healing can thicken, fuse and calcify rheumatic mitral leaflets. The autopsy image is needed to distinguish these changes from other valve disease.
A large transmural anterior infarct can heal with a thinned dyskinetic ventricular scar, predisposing to true ventricular aneurysm.
Varenicline partially activates alpha4beta2 nicotinic receptors, reducing withdrawal while limiting nicotine's reinforcing effect. Treatment choice accounts for tolerability and patient factors.
Sleepwalking is a non-REM arousal disorder with incomplete awareness and often poor recall. Full normal consciousness is not characteristic during an episode.
Delusional disorder often begins later than some other psychotic disorders. Age alone is not a diagnostic exclusion, and proposed risk factors require a defined population.
Ejaculation and orgasm are closely related components of the sexual response. Premature ejaculation concerns ejaculation timing and control, with associated distress, rather than desire alone.
The Confusion Assessment Method checks acute or fluctuating change and inattention with disorganised thinking or altered consciousness, supporting delirium identification.
Prominent hoarding symptoms can respond less well to standard OCD exposure-response prevention. Hoarding disorder is now distinct and may need tailored interventions.
Acrophobia denotes an excessive fear of heights. A phobia diagnosis additionally requires persistent disproportionate fear, avoidance or distress and meaningful functional consequences.
MHC II principally presents peptides from endosomal processing of extracellular material to CD4 T cells. MHC I usually presents endogenous peptides to CD8 cells, with recognised exceptions.
Visible haemagglutination can indicate a reaction without a fluorescent or enzyme-labelled antibody. The exact assay format matters because haemagglutination methods have several designs.

IgG2 contributes responses against polysaccharide antigens on encapsulated organisms. Recurrent infections warrant broader immune assessment; normal developmental subclass variation matters in young children.
Bacillus anthracis can cause an initially painless lesion progressing to a black eschar with oedema. Exposure and microbiological confirmation distinguish mimics.
Culture requires microbial growth and is not an immediate screening result. Urinalysis and microscopy provide faster clues, while culture guides identification and susceptibility.
Kirby-Bauer testing measures inhibition zones around antibiotic discs under standardised conditions. Breakpoints, organism and technique determine susceptibility interpretation.
CSF-VDRL is highly specific but incompletely sensitive in the appropriate clinical setting. Serum VDRL alone does not diagnose neurosyphilis; neurological assessment and CSF interpretation matter.
Contact precautions can reduce MRSA transmission in appropriate healthcare settings. Application follows current institutional infection-control guidance and does not replace standard precautions.
Meningococci are Gram-negative diplococci that may appear within neutrophils in CSF. The stain and laboratory evidence are needed to verify the pictured pathogen.
Mucicarmine stains the polysaccharide capsule of Cryptococcus. Antigen testing and other microbiological methods also support diagnosis in the appropriate specimen.
Japanese encephalitis virus circulates through mosquitoes and vertebrate amplifying hosts, including birds and pigs. Humans are generally incidental dead-end hosts.
Eating inadequately cooked infected freshwater crustaceans can transmit Paragonimus. Pulmonary infection may produce chronic cough and haemoptysis or rusty sputum.
Rubella virus is classified in Matonaviridae. Older classification systems placed it in Togaviridae.
The fertilised female mite burrows into superficial epidermis and deposits eggs. Attributing the characteristic burrow to the male is therefore the false statement.
Cryptosporidium can cause persistent watery diarrhoea in advanced immunodeficiency. The stool image and specific testing distinguish it from other opportunistic enteric pathogens.
Larval Taenia solium infection can cause brain cysts and seizures. MRI stage and lesion features are needed to distinguish cysticercosis from other intracranial lesions.
Antigenic drift and changing circulating strains require periodic influenza-vaccine composition updates. Strain selection is based on surveillance rather than the same formulation indefinitely.
Residual UGT1A1 activity in type II disease can increase with phenobarbital induction, lowering unconjugated bilirubin. Severity and testing distinguish it from other bilirubin disorders.

Established cerebral palsy is classified by persistent motor patterns such as spasticity, dyskinesia or ataxia. Early hypotonia can occur, so an absolute exclusion of every flaccid presentation is too broad.
Salt losses in cystic fibrosis can produce hypochloraemic hypokalaemic metabolic alkalosis. Hyperkalaemia is not the classic salt-depletion pattern.
Nonthrombocytopenic palpable purpura with joint and renal findings supports IgA vasculitis, formerly HSP. The photographed rash and clinical criteria still require confirmation.
Weight-for-length or height below minus three standard deviations is one SAM criterion. Low MUAC or bilateral nutritional oedema can independently establish it in appropriate age groups.
Retinochoroiditis is a major manifestation of congenital toxoplasmosis and may present later. Its rank as most common depends on case ascertainment and follow-up.
ABCC2 encodes the canalicular MRP2 transporter. Its dysfunction impairs biliary excretion of conjugated organic anions and causes predominantly conjugated hyperbilirubinaemia.
The right hand or wrist receives preductal arterial blood and is the usual site for neonatal preductal pulse-oximetry assessment.
Severe necrotising enterocolitis can cause metabolic acidosis through hypoperfusion and systemic illness. Metabolic alkalosis is not its characteristic systemic pattern.
Mother-to-child HIV transmission can occur during pregnancy, delivery or breastfeeding. Prevention and infant testing depend on maternal treatment and the exposure period.
Rising arterial oxygen tension and falling prostaglandin influence after birth promote ductus arteriosus constriction. Gestation and disease can alter this transition.
Thiamine deficiency impairs energy metabolism and can cause neuropathy and wet-beriberi cardiac failure with oedema. Clinical setting and competing causes require assessment.
Biliary atresia is a leading indication for paediatric liver transplantation in many registries. Ranking varies by age, region and transplant programme.
Reaching toward a presented object emerges during early infancy, often around four months in teaching tables. Milestone ranges vary and should be assessed across developmental domains.
Cyanosis scores zero; heart rate below one hundred, weak gasping, minimal grimace and some flexion each score one. The stated components therefore total four.
Patent ductus arteriosus and pulmonary-artery stenosis are characteristic congenital-rubella cardiac lesions. Other defects can occur and require echocardiographic assessment.
Tetralogy of Fallot can produce a boot-shaped cardiac silhouette from right-ventricular hypertrophy and reduced pulmonary-conus prominence. The radiograph must show the intended pattern.
Cyclophosphamide metabolites can damage urothelium and cause haemorrhagic cystitis; cumulative exposure also increases bladder-cancer risk. Prevention and monitoring depend on regimen.
A typical second-branchial-cleft cyst lies along the anterior sternocleidomastoid border near its upper-middle junction. Adult neck masses still require assessment for malignant mimics.
Dohlman's endoscopic approach divides the common wall between a pharyngeal pouch and oesophagus, treating selected Zenker diverticula.
Forearm muscle, often brachioradialis, is a possible parathyroid autotransplant site. Sternocleidomastoid is also used depending on the operation and monitoring needs.
Most rectal malignancies are adenocarcinomas arising from glandular epithelium. Calling adenocarcinoma a rare rectal-carcinoma variant is therefore false.
Severe ileus or fluid-filled bowel can produce relatively little visible gas, including in pancreatitis. A gasless film is nonspecific and cannot establish pancreatitis alone.
Cholesterol stones contain cholesterol monohydrate crystals, often mixed with other components. The most prevalent stone chemistry varies by region and clinical population.
CMV can produce large longitudinal or serpiginous oesophageal ulcers, especially with immunosuppression. Biopsy and appropriate viral testing distinguish it from HSV and other causes.
IPC section 193 historically concerned punishment for giving or fabricating false evidence. This entry describes the historical IPC provision.
Phenol is corrosive and gastric lavage is not a routine modern treatment.
Frotteurism involves sexual arousal from touching or rubbing against a nonconsenting person. A disorder diagnosis additionally requires the relevant behavioural or distress criteria.
Identical twins share much genetic material but develop distinct friction-ridge details because fetal development also influences fingerprints. Their prints are therefore not identical.
Injuries of differing ages can raise safeguarding concern but do not independently prove abuse. A trained assessment considers development, explanations, examination and alternative medical causes.

Recognition-based electrophysiological tests assess responses to familiar information. They cannot directly determine guilt or prove that a specific event occurred, and legal safeguards govern their use.
Soot, burning and powder tattooing support relatively close firing range, but their distribution depends on weapon, ammunition and intermediate targets. Examine the actual wound.
Postmortem ATP depletion affects cardiac and skeletal muscle. Descriptions of first biochemical onset differ from the clinically observed skeletal progression and cannot precisely time death.
The intermediate causal chain places cerebral metastasis below intracerebral haemorrhage and resulting bronchopneumonia, with the bronchial primary recorded further down as the underlying cause.
Prazosin counteracts alpha-adrenergic cardiovascular effects in appropriate scorpion envenomation protocols. It does not neutralise venom, and severity-directed supportive care remains essential.
Saturated sodium chloride has historical use for preserving selected viscera. Preservative choice depends on the suspected toxin and laboratory method; it is not suitable for every analysis.
Stretch depolarises vascular smooth muscle and promotes calcium entry, causing afferent arteriolar contraction. This helps stabilise renal flow against pressure changes.

Decerebrate posturing predominantly extends limbs through disordered brainstem motor control. Saying all muscles become uniformly rigid is an oversimplification, and the complete alternatives need review.
Decorticate posturing classically flexes the upper limbs and extends the lower limbs, reflecting loss of descending control above the red-nucleus level.
Conventional CPD-preserved red cells have a twenty-one-day shelf life, while CPDA-1 permits thirty-five days. Storage specifications depend on the collection system and regulatory standard.
Functional residual capacity is the volume remaining after normal expiration and equals expiratory reserve volume plus residual volume.
Dietary gums are generally classified as soluble fibre. Therefore selecting gums as not dietary fibre conflicts with standard nutritional classification; the remaining options require review.

At pontine level the medial lemniscus carries already-crossed dorsal-column sensory information. Injury causes contralateral loss of vibration, discriminative touch and proprioception below the lesion.
VIP contributes inhibitory enteric signalling and smooth-muscle relaxation ahead of a propagating intestinal contraction. Nitric oxide is another important inhibitory transmitter.
Increased venous return stretches atrial receptors and can increase heart rate through the Bainbridge reflex, with interaction from other cardiovascular reflexes.
LH stimulates Leydig cells to synthesise testosterone. Sertoli cells instead support spermatogenesis and produce factors including inhibin B.
A ureterocele is cystic dilatation of the distal ureter and can produce a cobra-head appearance on contrast imaging. The IVP image must confirm that sign.
Macula-densa sensing of distal sodium-chloride delivery adjusts afferent tone and renin signalling, helping regulate single-nephron filtration.
Agglutination with anti-A, anti-B and anti-D reagents determines forward ABO and RhD typing. The actual reaction pattern is required to verify O positive.
Ventral respiratory-group networks recruit expiratory motor output during active or forceful expiration. Quiet expiration is largely passive.
V2-receptor signalling promotes aquaporin-2 insertion into collecting-duct principal-cell apical membranes, increasing water reabsorption.
Postganglionic sympathetic fibres are predominantly small unmyelinated C fibres, which conduct more slowly than larger myelinated motor or sensory fibres.
Hepatic stellate, or Ito, cells store vitamin A in lipid droplets. Activation during liver injury can shift them toward a fibrogenic phenotype.
Plasma cells produce immunoglobulins. The liver synthesises many other plasma proteins, including albumin and numerous coagulation factors.
Hypoxia inhibits oxygen-sensitive potassium currents in carotid-body glomus cells, promoting depolarisation, calcium entry and transmitter release.
Spinothalamic fibres cross near their entry level, so cord hemisection produces contralateral pain-temperature loss below the lesion alongside ipsilateral dorsal-column and motor deficits.

Epidural bleeding lies between skull and dura, subdural bleeding between dura and arachnoid, and subarachnoid bleeding within the CSF-containing subarachnoid space. Intraparenchymal bleeding occurs within brain tissue.
A barium meal outlines upper gastrointestinal anatomy. The radiograph's contrast location and timing are needed to distinguish it from swallow, follow-through or other studies.
Diffusion-weighted MRI can detect restricted water diffusion early in acute cerebral ischaemia. Emergency imaging choice still depends on treatment timing and excluding haemorrhage without delay.
Disseminated tuberculosis can produce diffuse fine nodules on chest imaging. Other causes of a miliary pattern exist, requiring clinical and microbiological correlation.
The cerebellum lies in the posterior fossa behind the brainstem and coordinates movement and balance. The actual label and imaging plane determine the marked structure.
Iohexol is a nonionic water-soluble iodinated contrast agent. Suitability and route depend on the examination, renal assessment and previous contrast reactions.
Radiographic bowel-gas patterns reflect obstruction, ileus and other processes.
A reef or square knot uses opposing throws to create a balanced knot. The image must show throw direction before distinguishing it from a granny knot.
Tamoxifen modulates oestrogen receptors and antagonises oestrogen action in breast tissue. Treatment selection depends on receptor status and individual benefits and risks.
Many retrosternal goitres can be removed through a cervical approach. Extent, ectopic supply, malignancy and mediastinal anatomy may require a different or combined approach.
A cervical approach is often feasible for retrosternal goitre, but extensive mediastinal disease may need additional access. This source repeats the question at Q201 and Q202.

Chest-drain insertion uses a deliberately selected safe anatomical site and technique, avoiding neurovascular structures and underlying organs. A generic posterior intercostal instruction is insufficient and potentially unsafe.
A number-eleven blade has a pointed tip suited to selected stab incisions. The photographed blade must be confirmed before assigning its number.
Posterior dislocation commonly follows dashboard-type trauma and may present with a shortened internally rotated limb. Radiographs confirm direction and associated fracture before urgent management.
A Brodie abscess is a localised subacute osteomyelitic lesion, often metaphyseal with surrounding sclerosis. The radiograph is required to distinguish tumour and other lesions.

Gas-containing organs are particularly vulnerable to primary blast pressure waves. Solid liver tissue is relatively less susceptible to that mechanism, although other blast-related forces can still injure it.
The proximal scaphoid has vulnerable retrograde blood supply, increasing risks of avascular necrosis and nonunion after fracture.
A slow-growing mixed-consistency salivary mass can suggest pleomorphic adenoma. Location, imaging and tissue assessment are needed to distinguish other salivary tumours.
A painful arc often reflects subacromial impingement. A complete supraspinatus tear can instead cause marked weakness, but pain patterns alone cannot definitively exclude a tear.
A skin cyst with a punctum and keratinous contents often represents an epidermoid cyst, commonly miscalled sebaceous cyst. The photograph must establish its characteristics.
Shearing separates skin and subcutaneous tissue from deeper fascia, disrupting perforating vessels. The injury may be open or concealed beneath intact skin.

A biologic such as an anti-TNF agent may be added after inadequate response to appropriate conventional therapy. Existing deformity alone does not determine drug choice or replace infection screening.

An unsuccessful aspiration requires reassessment of localisation, contents and technique, often with ultrasound. Repeat image-guided aspiration may help, but persistent or complex collections may need other drainage.
Reduced bone strength can cause vertebral compression fractures. CT morphology and clinical assessment are needed; osteoporosis diagnosis is not established solely by an unspecified scan image.
Aberrant regeneration of auriculotemporal parasympathetic fibres toward cutaneous sweat glands produces gustatory sweating after parotid-region injury.
Extended curettage and grafting can treat selected benign aggressive bone lesions. The image and tissue diagnosis must establish the lesion before endorsing this operation.
Jersey finger avulses flexor digitorum profundus; mallet or baseball finger injures terminal extensor function. The individual images must be matched to the respective loss of movement.
Leg DVT commonly presents unilaterally. Bilateral thrombosis can occur, but describing most DVT as bilateral is incorrect.
A reversible competitive antagonist typically shifts an agonist curve rightward without reducing its achievable maximum. The plotted axes and responses are required to identify curve B.
CEAP clinical class C2 denotes varicose veins, generally at least three millimetres when measured upright. Oedema and skin changes belong to higher classes.
Brimonidine can cause serious central nervous system and respiratory depression in infants and young children. Its use is restricted by age-specific contraindications and warnings.
An apparent distribution volume much larger than body water suggests extensive tissue binding or sequestration relative to plasma concentration. It is not a literal anatomical fluid volume.
Phase II trials explore efficacy and dose in affected patients while continuing safety assessment. Phase III also assesses efficacy in larger confirmatory studies, so the label is not exclusive.
A transplant between genetically different individuals of the same species is an allograft, including a graft from a biological relative other than an identical twin.
The Revised Trauma Score uses Glasgow Coma Scale, systolic pressure and respiratory rate. Pulse rate is not one of its scored components.
Rivaroxaban is an oral direct factor Xa inhibitor that reduces thrombin generation. It differs from indirect heparin-mediated inhibition and vitamin-K antagonism.
A macrolide such as erythromycin is a recognised option for eradication in diphtheria carriers. Current public-health guidance, resistance and post-treatment cultures determine management.
Oseltamivir and zanamivir inhibit viral neuraminidase, reducing release of new influenza particles from infected cells. They do not directly block viral protein synthesis.
Carboprost is a prostaglandin F2-alpha analogue that stimulates uterine contraction. Its indication, route and contraindications must be distinguished from those of other prostaglandins.
Nicorandil opens ATP-sensitive potassium channels and has nitrate-like effects, promoting vascular relaxation. Its mechanism differs from a pure calcium-channel blocker.
Granisetron blocks 5-HT3 receptors and helps prevent chemotherapy-induced emesis. Best prophylaxis depends on emetic risk and often combines several drug classes.
Nasal polyps commonly associate with asthma and aspirin-exacerbated respiratory disease. The older intrinsic-asthma label is imprecise and does not cover every mechanism.
Teduglutide is a GLP-2 analogue that promotes intestinal adaptation and absorption. It is used for selected short-bowel-syndrome patients requiring parenteral support.
Cisatracurium generally releases less histamine than atracurium at clinical doses, reducing associated haemodynamic effects. Both require appropriate neuromuscular monitoring.
Oesophageal candidiasis is an AIDS-defining illness, whereas uncomplicated oral candidiasis alone is not. Both can indicate clinically important immune dysfunction.
Febuxostat inhibits xanthine oxidase and lowers urate production.
An HLA-matched healthy sibling is often a strong allogeneic donor candidate. ABO or Rh mismatch does not automatically exclude donation, and broader donor factors still matter.
Levofloxacin has near-complete oral bioavailability. Several other fluoroquinolones also have high values, so maximum requires checking the listed agents and formulation.
Triazoles inhibit fungal lanosterol 14-alpha-demethylase and impair ergosterol synthesis. Forming membrane pores describes polyene action, not the standard triazole mechanism.
Acitretin is highly teratogenic and pregnancy must be avoided for the required prolonged period after treatment, commonly three years. Six months is insufficient under standard labelling.
Advanced HIV with subacute dry cough and respiratory symptoms raises concern for Pneumocystis pneumonia. Imaging and organism-directed testing are needed to distinguish other causes.
Cilastatin inhibits renal dehydropeptidase I, reducing imipenem degradation and improving active drug exposure. It is not an antibacterial substitute itself.
Edrophonium was historically used in assessing myasthenic weakness, but can cause serious cholinergic effects. It is not a routine safe bedside shortcut for differentiating acute crises.

Classic GBS often progresses from leg weakness upward with reduced reflexes. Variants exist, but a descending pattern is not the usual teaching description and requires alternative diagnoses to be considered.

G-CSF products carry warnings about severe sickle-cell crises in affected patients. A blanket rule should be checked against current labelling and specialist risk assessment rather than assumed from this recall.
Splenectomy can provide durable response in selected persistent ITP. It is not universally the best initial treatment; bleeding risk, disease duration and medical options guide care.
Tolvaptan can increase free-water excretion in selected SIADH cases, but is not universal first-line treatment. Cause treatment, fluid measures and controlled sodium correction are essential.
Mitral obstruction raises left-atrial pressure and can enlarge the left atrium. Pulmonary vascular and right-heart changes may develop subsequently.
Intravenous mannitol can acutely lower markedly raised intraocular pressure through an osmotic effect. It is not routine chronic therapy for every glaucoma patient.
Imipenem can provoke seizures, particularly with high exposure, renal impairment or central nervous system disease. Dose adjustment and patient-specific risk matter.
Child-Pugh scoring uses bilirubin, albumin, coagulation, ascites and encephalopathy. Creatinine belongs to other liver-risk models rather than the standard Child-Pugh variables.
Prostaglandin E1 can maintain ductus arteriosus patency in selected duct-dependent congenital heart disease. Administration requires monitored specialist care.
An accessory atrioventricular pathway can conduct outside normal AV-nodal delay and produce ventricular pre-excitation. Calling it necessarily slower than the AV node is false.
Hypothermia can produce prominent J or Osborn waves at the QRS-ST junction. Other causes exist, so the ECG finding requires temperature and clinical correlation.
Insulin resistance in obesity often produces compensatory hyperinsulinaemia. Levels depend on beta-cell function and diabetes stage, so increased insulin is not universal.
A ventricular-origin tachyarrhythmia commonly has wide QRS complexes. The tracing is needed to confirm VT and distinguish other wide-complex rhythms.
Annual Blood Examination Rate measures the proportion of a population tested for malaria over a year. It reflects surveillance activity rather than test sensitivity or disease incidence alone.

Classical trigeminal neuralgia causes brief electric-shock-like attacks in a trigeminal distribution, often with tactile triggers. Deep continuous pain is less typical and warrants broader assessment.
A confounder must relate to exposure and outcome without being an intermediate. Equal distribution between groups generally reduces confounding from that factor rather than defining it.
Early diagnosis and prompt treatment are secondary-prevention measures. Whether a screening strategy is best depends on evidence, population and the distinction from primary risk reduction.

Clinical xerophthalmia in a child older than twelve months uses age-specific high-dose vitamin A with repeat dosing under recognised protocols. Confirm diagnosis, timing and prior doses rather than applying the schedule indiscriminately.
Approximately 68.3 percent of values in a normal distribution lie between one standard deviation below and above the mean.
For ages two to below twelve months, the IMCI fast-breathing threshold is fifty or more breaths per minute. More than fifty would wrongly exclude a rate of exactly fifty.
Adulteration of foodstuffs and other goods appears in the Constitution's Concurrent List. This concerns legislative competence, not the complete operational food-safety law.
Loss of colonic haustration producing a lead-pipe appearance is classically associated with chronic ulcerative colitis, rather than the typical skip-lesion Crohn pattern.
Acute inflammatory demyelinating polyneuropathy is common in many Western cohorts. Axonal variants are more frequent in some regions, so most common depends on geography and population.
Cushing ulcers are stress-related gastroduodenal ulcers associated with intracranial disease or injury. They differ from Curling ulcers classically associated with severe burns.
PNH clones lack GPI-anchored proteins including CD55 and CD59, making blood cells vulnerable to complement injury. Flow cytometry assesses this deficiency.

Adding sulfasalazine and hydroxychloroquine creates conventional triple therapy with methotrexate. Treatment escalation depends on disease activity, prior optimisation, prognostic factors and biologic alternatives.
Photosensitivity, oral ulcers and systemic symptoms can support SLE, but rash appearance and immunological assessment are needed. These findings alone do not establish every classification criterion.
Standing reduces ventricular filling and can increase dynamic left-ventricular outflow obstruction in hypertrophic cardiomyopathy, intensifying its murmur. Mitral-prolapse findings can also change.
A reduced FEV1/FVC ratio suggests airflow obstruction. Interpretation uses suitable reference limits and clinical context, with bronchodilator testing when indicated.

Calcitonin responds to calcium and is a marker of medullary thyroid disease. Hyperparathyroid hypercalcaemia can influence secretion, but it is not a specific diagnostic association without the alternatives and context.
Pneumonia is a major direct pulmonary cause of ARDS. If the question means a cause acting indirectly from the vascular side, it must say so; pneumonia is not a general noncause.
