Streptococcal surface adhesins interact with epithelial and extracellular-matrix proteins, including fibronectin. Lipoteichoic-acid-associated adherence is a traditional examination association, although several proteins contribute to actual colonisation.

Campylobacter can be acquired from unpasteurised milk and causes inflammatory diarrhoea that may become bloody. Its curved Gram-negative morphology and the exposure history support the recalled organism.

Aspergillus typically forms septate hyphae with acute-angle branching in tissue. This contrasts with the broader, sparsely septate hyphae more typical of mucormycosis; diagnosis still requires clinicopathological correlation.

Female Enterobius migrate to the perianal region at night to deposit eggs, producing characteristic nocturnal itching. A morning perianal adhesive-tape sample is more useful than routine stool examination for detecting the eggs.

Histoplasma appears as small yeasts, often within macrophages, and can cause a chronic pulmonary syndrome. Narrow-based budding alone is not specific because other yeasts, notably Cryptococcus, may share that feature.

references.title: CDC Emerging Infectious Diseases: Histoplasma diagnosis

records.explanation: Nocardia forms branching Gram-positive filaments and is variably or weakly acid-fast. It can disseminate from pulmonary infection to form brain abscesses, especially in susceptible hosts.

The terminal complement components form the membrane attack complex. Deficiency predisposes to recurrent invasive Neisseria infection; pathway screening and targeted component testing can investigate the defect.
Adult filarial worms and the associated inflammatory response can damage lymphatic drainage. Chronic lymphatic obstruction then causes lymphoedema and, in severe cases, elephantiasis.

Leptospira exposure is associated with animal-urine-contaminated water, including occupational sewage contact. Severe disease can combine jaundice, acute kidney injury and conjunctival suffusion, a pattern traditionally called Weil disease.

Established infection before pregnancy usually carries very low congenital-transmission risk in an immunocompetent woman. IgG alone does not date an infection precisely; IgM, avidity and reference testing may be needed if recent infection is suspected.

Fibrous amniotic bands can constrict or amputate developing digits and limbs. This mechanism explains an absent digit, but the specific anatomy and other malformations should be reviewed before assigning the diagnosis.

The cardinal-uterosacral ligament complex provides major support to the cervix and upper vagina. Childbirth-related injury to this support and the pelvic floor contributes to uterine descent and prolapse.

Serous ovarian carcinomas can present with abdominal fullness and elevated CA-125. Neither CA-125 elevation nor symptoms alone distinguishes histological subtype; the gross and microscopic appearance provides important diagnostic evidence.

The standard Pritchard loading regimen combines 4 g magnesium sulfate intravenously with 10 g intramuscularly, divided between the buttocks, for a total of 14 g. Administration requires toxicity monitoring and an appropriate obstetric protocol.

Repair normally proceeds from the vaginal mucosa and its apex to the perineal muscles and then the skin. Adequate haemostasis and restoration of tissue alignment matter; the anal sphincter must be assessed separately for an associated tear.

Lovset rotation is used to deliver extended fetal arms during an assisted breech birth. It brings a shoulder anteriorly so the arm can be released; this differs from manoeuvres aimed primarily at flexing the after-coming head.

Controlled cord traction combines gentle traction on the cord with counterpressure that stabilises the contracted uterus. It assists placental delivery when performed correctly by a trained attendant and should not be confused with forceful unopposed cord pulling.

Postmenopausal bleeding warrants assessment of vaginal, cervical and endometrial causes. Examination and appropriate endometrial evaluation are needed; cervical cytology alone cannot exclude endometrial cancer, and biopsy decisions depend on the clinical context.

references.title: ACOG: updated postmenopausal bleeding guidance, April 2026

records.explanation: Postmenopausal bleeding is an important presenting symptom of endometrial carcinoma. Histopathology establishes the diagnosis; undergoing hysterectomy by itself does not distinguish cancer from the other uterine conditions listed.

references.title: ACOG: updated postmenopausal bleeding guidance, April 2026

records.explanation: Low-molecular-weight heparin is widely used for postpartum venous-thromboembolism prophylaxis or treatment. Warfarin is also compatible with breastfeeding in appropriate situations, so drug choice depends on the indication and clinical circumstances.

Amenorrhoea before age forty with elevated gonadotropins and low ovarian-reserve markers suggests primary ovarian insufficiency. Diagnosis requires the appropriate menstrual history and evaluation of other causes rather than relying on AMH alone.

Endometrial sampling is indicated in many patients aged forty-five or older with abnormal uterine bleeding to assess hyperplasia or malignancy. A single premenopausal endometrial-thickness measurement is influenced by menstrual phase and does not replace tissue assessment.

references.title: ACOG: updated postmenopausal bleeding guidance, April 2026

records.explanation: For atonic postpartum haemorrhage not controlled by initial treatment, uterine balloon tamponade can compress bleeding vessels. It should be used within a functioning haemorrhage pathway with resuscitation, monitoring and timely access to surgery if needed.
McRoberts positioning and suprapubic pressure are initial shoulder-dystocia manoeuvres. Further release manoeuvres are selected by trained clinicians according to the response and circumstances.

records.topic: Fetal bradycardia during labour after caesarean
records.explanation: Persistent fetal bradycardia during labour after a previous caesarean demands urgent assessment for fetal compromise and uterine rupture. If rapid safe vaginal birth is not imminent, emergency operative delivery may be necessary.
The corpus luteum secretes progesterone and estradiol in the mid-luteal phase. Negative feedback suppresses gonadotropins while progesterone supports the secretory endometrium.

Cord prolapse requires immediate measures to relieve cord compression while arranging expedited birth. Elevating the presenting part and appropriate positioning can protect perfusion; caesarean is usually needed if vaginal birth is not immediately achievable.

Tumour-related hydronephrosis or a nonfunctioning kidney is a feature of FIGO stage IIIB cervical cancer, unless attributable to another cause. Nodal disease may additionally determine stage IIIC under the applicable staging system.

Bluish discoloration of the vagina or cervix is a probable clinical sign of pregnancy. Amenorrhoea, nausea and skin changes are presumptive clues; positive signs include direct evidence of the fetus such as ultrasound identification.
Adenomyosis consists of endometrial glands and stroma within the myometrium and may cause dysmenorrhoea and heavy bleeding. MRI features such as an abnormal junctional zone can support the diagnosis.

Once an embryo is visible, crown-rump length is the preferred early ultrasound measurement for gestational dating. Later biometric parameters have wider dating uncertainty and should not replace a reliable early measurement without a clinical reason.

An initially nonreactive NST may reflect a fetal sleep cycle, so monitoring can be extended to a total of about forty minutes in an otherwise reassuring situation. Persistent nonreactivity or other concerning findings require further assessment.

Pseudoexfoliation produces flaky fibrillar deposits on anterior-segment structures, including the lens capsule. It is associated with glaucoma and zonular weakness, making recognition important before cataract surgery.

INTACS segments alter corneal geometry to reduce irregularity in selected keratoconus cases. They do not replace treatment directed at progression, and suitability depends on corneal thickness, scarring and other clinical factors.
A longstanding slowly enlarging painless mass near an orbital suture is compatible with a dermoid cyst. Imaging helps define its extent and exclude deeper extension before surgical management.

Loss of corneal endothelial cells impairs fluid pumping and can cause stromal and epithelial oedema. Corneal guttae and eventual bullous keratopathy are characteristic findings in Fuchs endothelial dystrophy.

Infection can spread from the ethmoid sinuses through the thin medial orbital wall into the orbit. Orbital disease may impair eye movements or vision and requires systemic treatment and urgent specialist assessment.

Simultaneous perception means perceiving images from both eyes, fusion combines them into one percept, and stereopsis provides binocular depth perception. The test images must be identified before assigning these functions to labels A and B.

Inflammatory back pain and anterior uveitis raise suspicion for axial spondyloarthritis. MRI of the sacroiliac joints can reveal active inflammation before structural abnormalities are visible on plain radiographs.

Spondylolisthesis is displacement of one vertebral body relative to the adjacent vertebra. Spondylolysis refers to a pars defect and can exist without a slip, so imaging must establish which abnormality is present.

Perthes disease is osteonecrosis of the developing femoral head and may present with a limp. In an eleven-year-old, slipped capital femoral epiphysis is also a relevant differential; radiographic findings must decide between them.

Disproportionate pain and pain on passive stretch after a tibial fracture are concerning for compartment syndrome. Pulses may remain palpable because tissue perfusion fails before major arterial flow; urgent surgical assessment and decompression are required when diagnosed.

Respiratory deterioration, neurological abnormalities and a petechial rash after long-bone fractures suggest fat embolism syndrome. The usual delay of one to three days supports the diagnosis, although competing causes of hypoxia must be assessed.

Calcium pyrophosphate crystals are typically rhomboid and weakly positively birefringent under compensated polarised microscopy. Monosodium urate crystals are usually needle-shaped and strongly negatively birefringent.
Apoptosis involves executioner caspases. Pyroptosis uses inflammatory caspases and gasdermin pores, while necroptosis is regulated through the RIPK-MLKL pathway.

Antimitochondrial antibodies are strongly associated with primary biliary cholangitis, an autoimmune disease of small intrahepatic bile ducts. The diagnosis integrates cholestatic liver tests, serology and other clinical evidence.

Marfan syndrome usually shows autosomal-dominant inheritance, so an affected parent may transmit the condition to children of either sex. The actual pedigree is necessary to distinguish this pattern from mitochondrial, X-linked and imprinting disorders.

Peripheral-blood flow cytometry identifies the clonal B-cell population and its surface-marker pattern in typical CLL. It is central to distinguishing CLL from reactive lymphocytosis and other mature lymphoid neoplasms.

Focal nodular hyperplasia is a benign hepatic lesion that can show a central stellate scar and characteristic vascular architecture. Imaging or pathology must distinguish it from adenoma, hepatocellular carcinoma and metastasis.

Sarcoidosis can cause non-necrotising granulomas with multinucleated giant cells containing asteroid bodies. These inclusions are supportive but not specific, so infections and other granulomatous causes must be considered.
Pathogenic FBN1 variants impair fibrillin-1-containing microfibrils in connective tissue. Long-limbed habitus, ectopia lentis and aortic disease are major manifestations that support Marfan syndrome.
Schwannomas characteristically contain compact Antoni A areas and looser Antoni B areas. Nuclear palisading in Antoni A tissue produces Verocay bodies, supporting a Schwann-cell tumour.
A suprasellar mass with growth disturbance and visual symptoms in a child suggests craniopharyngioma. Wet keratin is a characteristic pathological feature of the adamantinomatous type.

Flow cytometry analyses labelled cells individually as they pass through a detector. Fluorescent antibodies allow simultaneous measurement of multiple surface or intracellular markers and help define abnormal cell populations.

Anti-Scl-70 targets topoisomerase I and is associated with systemic sclerosis, especially increased risk of interstitial lung disease. Antibody status supports risk assessment but does not replace pulmonary screening.

Seminoma commonly forms a homogeneous pale testicular mass with limited haemorrhage or necrosis. Typical histology shows large germ cells separated by fibrous septa with lymphocytes; pathology is needed for definitive classification.

The t(14;18) rearrangement places BCL2 under immunoglobulin-heavy-chain regulatory influence, reducing apoptosis. A germinal-centre phenotype with CD10 expression and follicles containing centrocytes and centroblasts supports follicular lymphoma.

Abnormal promyelocytes with bundles of Auer rods suggest acute promyelocytic leukaemia. The characteristic t(15;17) produces a PML-RARA fusion; urgent recognition matters because severe coagulopathy can accompany presentation.

Autoimmune lymphocytic injury to lacrimal and salivary glands reduces secretion, producing dry eyes and dry mouth. Anti-Ro and anti-La antibodies support the diagnosis in the appropriate clinical context.

Medullary thyroid carcinoma arises from parafollicular C cells. Tumour-associated amyloid derives from calcitonin-related material, distinguishing its stromal deposits from the usual morphology of follicular-derived thyroid cancers.

The historical AML M3 category corresponds to acute promyelocytic leukaemia, most often driven by PML-RARA from t(15;17). This fusion blocks normal differentiation and explains the role of differentiation-directed treatment.

A benzodiazepine is a rescue treatment for a prolonged ongoing convulsive seizure, including a febrile seizure. A brief seizure that has already stopped does not automatically require an anticonvulsant dose.

ADA deficiency causes accumulation of metabolites toxic to lymphocytes. Severe loss of immune-cell function can produce combined immunodeficiency with recurrent opportunistic infections, poor growth and early presentation.

Progressive external ophthalmoplegia, pigmentary retinopathy and cardiac conduction disease form the classic Kearns-Sayre pattern. It is associated with mitochondrial DNA deletions, which are frequently sporadic rather than showing a straightforward multigenerational pattern.

For a responsive child with severe foreign-body airway obstruction, current AHA guidance alternates five back blows with five abdominal thrusts. Management changes if the child can cough effectively or becomes unresponsive.

Hexosaminidase A deficiency prevents normal GM2 ganglioside degradation, causing neuronal accumulation and progressive neurodegeneration. A cherry-red macula can be a diagnostic clue, although it also occurs in other storage diseases.

Alpha-L-iduronidase normally participates in degradation of dermatan sulfate and heparan sulfate. Deficiency causes their lysosomal storage in mucopolysaccharidosis type I, explaining coarse features and multisystem disease.

Complementary foods are introduced at six months in small amounts and gradually increased while breastfeeding continues. Guidance for breastfed infants aged six to eight months generally uses two to three meals daily, adjusted for the child and food consistency.

The cited NACO guidance classifies maternal viral load above 1000 copies/mL near delivery as a high-risk exposure. Its specified case-based regimen uses infant nevirapine plus zidovudine for twelve weeks, with infant-feeding counselling and follow-up testing.

references.title: NACO: National HIV Care and Treatment Guidelines 2021

records.explanation: CKD can impair phosphate excretion and vitamin D activation, disrupting bone mineralisation. Management considers serial calcium, phosphate, PTH and vitamin D results; phosphate-lowering treatment and calcium exposure must be individualised.

A diaphragmatic defect can allow abdominal viscera into the thorax, compressing the developing lung and causing neonatal respiratory distress. Chest imaging may show intrathoracic bowel and mediastinal shift.
Benralizumab binds the alpha subunit of the interleukin-5 receptor and promotes depletion of eosinophils. Its target is IL-5 receptor alpha, rather than free circulating IL-5 itself.

Appropriate close contacts of invasive meningococcal disease require prompt prophylaxis. Ciprofloxacin is an established option where local susceptibility supports it, but resistance, pregnancy and other circumstances may favour a different recommended agent.

Large chloride loads from 0.9% saline can reduce the strong-ion difference and produce normal-anion-gap hyperchloraemic metabolic acidosis. The risk depends on the volume and the patient's renal and physiological context.

Amiodarone has multiple electrophysiological effects, with potassium-channel blockade prolonging repolarisation and action-potential duration. This is the basis of its class III association with phase 3, although it also affects other channels and receptors.

Preoperative preparation usually establishes adequate alpha blockade before adding a beta blocker when necessary. Phenoxybenzamine is a recognised option; beta-predominant blockade before adequate alpha blockade can worsen vasoconstriction and hypertension.

Propranolol is an established migraine-preventive drug, while triptans and ergot derivatives primarily treat attacks. Topiramate is also an established preventive option, so comorbidities and contraindications determine the individual choice.

Pegloticase is a pegylated uricase that oxidises uric acid to the more soluble allantoin. Its usual clinical role is refractory chronic gout; rasburicase is the uricase more commonly used in tumour-lysis management.

Metoclopramide enhances upper gastrointestinal motility and can increase lower-oesophageal-sphincter tone. Acid suppressants lower acid exposure but do not share this direct prokinetic mechanism; metoclopramide's neurological adverse effects limit use.

Some drugs can provoke lichenoid eruptions or other oral lesions that burn with spicy foods. Diagnosis requires the lesion's morphology, medication timeline and exclusion of alternative causes rather than assigning causation from a drug list alone.

Thiazides increase renal calcium reabsorption and usually reduce urinary calcium excretion. This is the relevant pharmacological basis for selected calcium-stone prevention settings; electrolyte effects and the indication still require individual assessment.

BPaLM combines bedaquiline, pretomanid, linezolid and moxifloxacin for eligible drug-resistant TB. Treatment selection depends on resistance and eligibility, with monitoring for drug-specific toxicity and for HIV-associated immune reconstitution when ART is initiated.

An alveolus that remains ventilated but loses perfusion develops an extremely high ventilation-perfusion ratio, approaching dead space. The letter identifying that region depends on the axes and labels of the supplied graph.

With zero net filtration, 18 minus interstitial hydrostatic pressure minus 27 plus 7 equals zero. Rearranging gives an interstitial hydrostatic pressure of minus 2 mmHg under the stated simplified Starling model.

Hypobaric hypoxia triggers cerebral vascular responses and contributes to acute mountain sickness symptoms such as headache and nausea. Pulmonary hypoxic vasoconstriction is a different response and is important in high-altitude pulmonary oedema.

A sustained glucose rise produces an early insulin burst from readily releasable granules, followed by a slower sustained phase involving recruitment and synthesis. This biphasic response is more precise than describing insulin as a single transient peak.

Maximum active force occurs at a sarcomere length that permits optimal actin-myosin overlap. Excessive shortening or stretch reduces productive cross-bridge interactions, while passive tension behaves differently from active tension.

Primary adrenal insufficiency can reduce both cortisol and aldosterone. Renal sodium loss, volume depletion and associated electrolyte disturbances help explain fatigue, cramps and a strong desire for salt.

references.title: NIDDK: adrenal insufficiency symptoms and causes

records.explanation: Hypoxia stimulates ventilation at altitude, increasing carbon dioxide elimination. The immediate acid-base effect is respiratory alkalosis; renal bicarbonate excretion contributes to acclimatisation over time.

Excess prolactin suppresses hypothalamic GnRH pulsatility, reducing gonadotropin support for normal ovarian function and causing amenorrhoea. This mechanism can accompany galactorrhoea in a prolactinoma.

Delayed repetitive orofacial and choreiform movements after prolonged dopamine-receptor blockade suggest tardive dyskinesia. VMAT2 inhibitors such as valbenazine can treat appropriate cases after clinical confirmation and review of the causative regimen.

Delusional perception assigns an abnormal, personally significant delusional meaning to a real sensory event. Seeing actual birds and interpreting their flight as divine instructions differs from seeing birds that are not present.

Pervasive perfectionism, rigidity and preoccupation with order can impair function in obsessive-compulsive personality disorder. These traits are often experienced as appropriate by the person, unlike the unwanted intrusive obsessions typical of OCD.

Unexpected travel accompanied by autobiographical amnesia or loss of identity fits the fugue presentation of dissociative amnesia. Substance effects, neurological disease and other causes must be excluded before attributing the episode to dissociation.

Trauma-related intrusion, dissociation and associated symptoms occurring from three days to one month after a qualifying trauma can fit acute stress disorder. PTSD requires persistence beyond one month, with the appropriate symptom pattern.

Psychotic symptoms require assessment of diagnosis, risk, capacity and the relevant legal questions. Fitness to stand trial concerns the person's ability to understand and participate in proceedings and is separate from criminal responsibility at the time of an offence.

Non-invasive imaging can demonstrate pelviureteric-junction obstruction, while functional studies help assess drainage and renal contribution. The appropriate interpretation depends on whether the image is ultrasound, MR urography, renography or another test.
Lobar collapse causes loss of lung volume, often with fissural displacement and other signs of retraction. Consolidation primarily fills airspaces and does not necessarily cause the same volume loss.
Meningiomas are typically extra-axial tumours and may have a broad dural attachment and characteristic enhancement. Headache alone cannot distinguish them from glioma and other intracranial masses.

High-resolution oesophageal manometry characterises lower-sphincter relaxation and oesophageal motility and is central to confirming achalasia. Endoscopy is also important to exclude mechanical obstruction or pseudoachalasia.

CT pulmonary angiography can directly demonstrate pulmonary arterial filling defects. Postoperative dyspnoea requires urgent risk assessment; test selection depends on haemodynamic stability, renal function, contraindications and clinical probability.

Phenoxybenzamine provides nonselective alpha-adrenergic blockade to reduce catecholamine-mediated vasoconstriction before surgery. Adequate preparation also addresses volume depletion, with beta blockade added only after effective alpha blockade when indicated.
The inferior vena cava lies posterior to portions of the duodenum and can be injured during difficult dissection. The exact vessel at risk depends on the duodenal segment and operative plane.

Wet gangrene involves tissue necrosis complicated by infection and usually swelling or moist tissue changes. Dry gangrene is more characteristically desiccated and demarcated; a clinical image and context are necessary to distinguish them.

Breast-cancer staging distinguishes tumour, nodal and metastatic categories from the overall stage group. T4d denotes inflammatory breast cancer, while overall stage IV indicates distant metastatic disease.
A carotid body paraganglioma can separate the internal and external carotid arteries, producing the lyre sign. A slowly enlarging mass near the carotid bifurcation fits this vascular tumour pattern.
A surgeon's knot adds an extra initial throw to increase friction while securing the knot. Distinguishing it from a square or granny knot requires checking the actual crossing and throw pattern.

Penetrating abdominal injury with haemodynamic instability and peritoneal signs usually requires urgent operative exploration. Diagnostic imaging should not create a harmful delay when the need for emergency surgery is already established.

An intersphincteric fistula tracks in the plane between the internal and external anal sphincters. Other Parks categories cross or extend around the external sphincter differently, so the tract diagram determines the classification.

Sustained venous hypertension can cause stasis dermatitis, haemosiderin pigmentation and lipodermatosclerosis. Ulceration may develop, so the absence of ulcers is not a defining feature of chronic venous disease.
Polydioxanone is a synthetic absorbable monofilament suture. Its relatively prolonged strength retention can be useful when tissues need longer support; it is not a natural collagen-derived material.

Pathological phimosis involves a scarred or diseased narrowing that prevents appropriate retraction and may cause symptoms. Nonretractility and ballooning can also occur physiologically at age three, so examination is needed before diagnosing true pathological phimosis.

Debridement removes nonviable tissue to assess the wound and support healing or graft preparation. Escharotomy instead releases a constricting eschar when it compromises circulation or ventilation; the pictured action determines which procedure is shown.

Skin of the anal margin and the canal below the dentate line drains prominently to superficial inguinal nodes. More proximal drainage follows different pelvic pathways, so precise tumour location determines the nodal pattern.

Ultrasound uses mechanical sound waves rather than ionising radiation, so it does not fall under the same AERB radiation-equipment licensing framework as X-ray devices. Other laws governing ultrasound practice still apply.

references.title: AERB bulletin: ultrasound and MRI outside ionising-radiation remit

records.explanation: A levonorgestrel intrauterine system can reduce menstrual bleeding while preserving the uterus. Suitability depends on uterine-cavity anatomy, fibroid characteristics and contraindications; substantial cavity distortion may make it inappropriate.

Fluid accumulation in the superficial lamina propria of the vocal folds causes polypoid swelling and a lowered voice pitch. Smoking is a strong association; persistent hoarseness still requires assessment for malignancy.

Contrast-enhanced MRI of the internal auditory canals and cerebellopontine angle is the preferred imaging approach for a suspected vestibular schwannoma or other retrocochlear lesion. It evaluates soft tissue more effectively than a routine temporal-bone CT.

Juvenile nasopharyngeal angiofibroma contains abnormal vascular channels with deficient muscular walls. Their limited ability to constrict contributes to profuse bleeding, making unplanned biopsy hazardous.

Stapes fixation causes conductive hearing loss and can produce an apparent bone-conduction depression near 2 kHz, called the Carhart notch. This mechanical effect is a characteristic clue to otosclerosis.

Bilateral nutritional oedema or a very low mid-upper-arm circumference can identify severe acute malnutrition in this age group. The need for inpatient care depends on complications, appetite, alertness and oedema severity.

Low phosphate with inappropriately reduced renal phosphate reabsorption supports phosphate-wasting rickets. X-linked hypophosphataemia is one cause, but other inherited and acquired renal tubular disorders need consideration.

Adenosine can terminate AV-node-dependent supraventricular tachycardia by transiently blocking AV conduction. In a stable child, the algorithm includes assessment and appropriate vagal manoeuvres before drug treatment when feasible.

A persistent audible PDA may be closed to address ongoing shunting and associated risks. Catheter closure is often feasible, while the decision for a tiny or silent duct depends on haemodynamics and specialist assessment.

A nephritic presentation after a latent interval following streptococcal infection fits poststreptococcal glomerulonephritis. Endocapillary inflammation with neutrophils supports the diagnosis alongside complement and evidence of preceding infection.

Low calcium despite elevated PTH suggests resistance to PTH rather than deficient secretion. Pseudohypoparathyroidism is one cause, but renal failure, vitamin D deficiency and the phosphate pattern must be assessed.
The spinal accessory nerve traverses the posterior triangle and supplies trapezius. Injury can impair shoulder shrug and upward scapular rotation, limiting overhead arm elevation.

The urinary system develops from intermediate mesoderm. The definitive kidney forms through interaction between the ureteric bud and metanephric mesenchyme, which have distinct contributions to its structures.

Acute fluctuating inattention and confusion after surgery suggest delirium. The Confusion Assessment Method evaluates its defining features; tools designed mainly for chronic cognitive impairment are less suited to this immediate question.

Naloxone competitively antagonises opioid receptors and can reverse opioid-induced respiratory depression. Airway and ventilation support remain essential, and recurrent toxicity may require further monitored treatment.

Tremor, dysarthria and ataxia can indicate lithium neurotoxicity. Assessment includes serum lithium, renal function, hydration, interacting drugs and the clinical course; the prescribed daily dose alone cannot exclude toxicity.

Odd beliefs, eccentric behaviour and persistent interpersonal difficulties can occur in schizotypal personality disorder. The diagnosis requires a pervasive pattern and distinction from psychosis, developmental conditions and culturally shared beliefs.

Vasopressin is synthesised mainly in the supraoptic and paraventricular nuclei and released from the posterior pituitary. Damage along this system can cause large volumes of dilute urine and compensatory thirst.

A salt-transport defect in the thick ascending limb can produce hypokalaemic metabolic alkalosis with hypercalciuria, a Bartter-type pattern. Distal convoluted-tubule disorders such as Gitelman syndrome more typically produce hypocalciuria.
A homogeneous germ-cell tumour with clear cells, fibrous septa and lymphocytes supports seminoma. OCT3/4 and c-KIT expression are useful elements of the immunophenotypic pattern.

Small hyperchromatic cells with scant cytoplasm, nuclear moulding, necrosis and a neuroendocrine marker pattern support small-cell lung carcinoma. Central location and smoking history provide additional clinical context.

Leaf-like stromal projections and increased stromal cellularity identify the phyllodes family of fibroepithelial breast tumours. Grading additionally assesses atypia, mitoses, stromal overgrowth and tumour margins.
No eye opening scores E1, inappropriate words score V3, and withdrawal from pain scores M4. Their sum is 1 plus 3 plus 4, giving a total GCS of 8.
Vericiguat stimulates soluble guanylate cyclase, increasing cyclic GMP signalling. It does not act by inhibiting PDE5 or neprilysin; its clinical use depends on the relevant heart-failure indication.

CD8-positive cytotoxic T cells recognise peptide antigen presented by MHC class I. Loss of MHC I can impair this recognition, although it may also increase susceptibility to natural-killer-cell responses.

Sexual-assault assessment should be trauma-informed and performed by an appropriately trained clinician. Hymenal appearance alone does not establish whether assault occurred, and a normal examination does not exclude abuse.

records.explanation: Cholera toxin increases intracellular cyclic AMP signalling, promoting CFTR-mediated chloride secretion. Water and electrolytes follow into the intestinal lumen, producing profuse secretory diarrhoea.

Mirabegron activates beta-3 adrenergic receptors in the detrusor, promoting bladder relaxation during storage. Its mechanism differs from antimuscarinic drugs, and blood-pressure effects need consideration.

Nitazoxanide is an active treatment option for giardiasis. Apparent metronidazole failure first requires confirmation of persistent infection, adequate treatment, adherence and reinfection risk; genuinely refractory infection may need a different or combined regimen.

Monobenzone can depigment remaining normally pigmented skin in selected people with very extensive vitiligo. The effect can be permanent and extend beyond application sites, so this is a specialist decision requiring informed discussion.

Severe sepsis can cause bilateral adrenal haemorrhage and acute adrenal failure, producing profound shock and electrolyte abnormalities. This pattern is called Waterhouse-Friderichsen syndrome and needs urgent treatment of both sepsis and adrenal insufficiency.

Vero-cell cytotoxicity assays can demonstrate biologically active Shiga toxin and serve as a historical reference method. Contemporary clinical diagnosis commonly uses stool culture plus assays for Shiga toxin or its genes.

records.explanation: Magnesium deficiency increases renal potassium loss and can prevent potassium correction despite replacement. Persistent hypokalaemia therefore requires checking and addressing magnesium as well as the underlying losses.

For a patient with confirmed primary aldosteronism who is considering surgery, adrenal venous sampling can distinguish unilateral from bilateral secretion. CT is also part of assessment, but a nodule alone may not identify the functional source.

Insulin shifts potassium into cells and may precipitate dangerous hypokalaemia. When potassium is already substantially low, potassium replacement and close monitoring take priority before further insulin according to the relevant DKA protocol.

CT pulmonary angiography can visualise pulmonary arterial emboli. In a clinically likely case, a D-dimer alone does not confirm the diagnosis; imaging choice still depends on stability and contraindications.

A stable patient with a localised appendiceal inflammatory mass may be managed initially with antibiotics and observation, sometimes with drainage of an associated abscess. Selected centres may use early laparoscopic treatment based on expertise and patient factors.

Placenta praevia can cause painless third-trimester vaginal bleeding because placental tissue lies near or over the cervical opening. Ultrasound establishes placental position; digital vaginal examination is avoided until praevia has been excluded.

Subglottic upper-airway inflammation produces the barking cough, hoarseness and inspiratory stridor of croup. Severity assessment depends on stridor at rest, work of breathing and the child's overall condition.

Aminoglycosides can injure renal tubular cells and the auditory or vestibular apparatus. Drug selection, dosing and monitoring account for renal function, exposure and other nephrotoxic or ototoxic medicines.

Antibiotic disruption of intestinal flora can permit toxigenic Clostridioides difficile to proliferate. Diarrhoea requires clinical assessment and appropriate testing; colonisation alone does not establish symptomatic infection.

Keratin pearls are concentric keratin collections formed by differentiating malignant squamous cells. They support a keratinising squamous-cell carcinoma when interpreted with the rest of the histology.
Point prevalence is the proportion of a defined population with a condition at a particular time. Incidence instead counts new cases over a specified period or person-time.
Phosphofructokinase-1 converts fructose-6-phosphate to fructose-1,6-bisphosphate and is a major regulatory step of glycolysis. It responds to the cell's energy state and to fructose-2,6-bisphosphate.
A rightward shift reduces haemoglobin's oxygen affinity at a given partial pressure. This facilitates unloading to tissues, as occurs with increased temperature, carbon dioxide, acidity or 2,3-BPG.
The axillary nerve passes around the surgical neck of the humerus with the posterior circumflex humeral artery. Injury can weaken the deltoid and impair sensation over the lateral shoulder.

Major bleeding on warfarin requires urgent reversal of the anticoagulant effect. Intravenous vitamin K provides sustained correction, while appropriate factor replacement supplies faster reversal under an emergency protocol.

Seizures attributable to severe hyponatraemia may require carefully monitored hypertonic saline to obtain an initial limited sodium rise. Subsequent correction must remain controlled because excessive correction risks osmotic demyelination.
Noncontrast brain CT rapidly identifies intracranial haemorrhage and major alternative diagnoses. This distinction is essential before choosing acute reperfusion or antithrombotic treatment pathways.
